name: page preview
background: none by default; var(--surface) on the thumb (or the whole card if it has no thumb)
border: no border; a 1px ring via box-shadow (var(--card-ring)) plus a soft drop shadow, not border-color
nesting: sits in a .wall / .page-previews grid (the index page's body); holds a thumb (a shrunk live render or an image) and a title+description, nothing nested inside
notes: the most common card on the whole site — every directory index is a wall of these. /imagine/gallery and /layouts/browse reskin it (gal-flat, std-browse) instead of inventing a new card.

name: card / surface
border: border-inline-start: 3px solid var(--card-edge, transparent) — a left stripe, not a full border
nesting: the base class other cards extend or sit inside (ux-content-section.card, framework.css's own doc demos); a plain .card can hold any content, including another .card
notes: the framework's one shared card primitive — everything else in this file is a variant or a sibling of this rule, not a separate system. Page.class.js even aliases surface: "card" so a page's own preview can ask for this look directly.

name: chip / pill
background: var(--wash) (var(--fill-a04) or var(--fill-a08) in ai2.css's versions)
radius: .3em, sometimes 1em (fully round) for a status dot
nesting: always inline, inside a row of other chips or beside text in a card's header; never holds another card
notes: the smallest 'card' on the site — a one-word background tag. The same look (wash/fill background, small radius, tight padding) is hand-rewritten in at least 6 files (ux/Content, ai2, decision) instead of sharing one class — see findings.md.

name: chat bubble
background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--prim) 22%, transparent) [you] / color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 10%, transparent) [reply]
padding: inherited from a shared .chatbox-msg rule (not re-measured here)
nesting: sits in a scrolling column of messages; never nests another card
notes: the one card kind on the site whose background is a tint of the ACCENT color rather than --surface/--wash — every other kind in this inventory uses a neutral ground.

name: icon card (icard)
background: var(--surface); turns var(--wash) when nested inside a .ux-content-section.card so the two grounds read apart
padding: not set directly here — comes from the flex gap (.4em) around centered content
border: 1px solid var(--line) (removed when nested in a .card section)
nesting: several sit in a .ux-content-icards flex row, which itself sits inside an optional .ux-content-section.card — the one place in the inventory where a card visibly nests one level inside another
notes: used for Concepts tiles; the comment at content.css:181 states the rule the owner wants generalized: a section with a background is the white ground, its child cards switch to wash so nesting still reads.

name: AI2 rail row
background: none at rest; var(--fill-a04) on hover; var(--surface) when active/in-path
padding: var(--pad-card) — explicitly reuses .card's own padding value (ai2.css:320 comment)
radius: 0 — rows sit flush, divided by a 1px border-block-end
border: 1px solid var(--line) bottom only, plus a 3px left accent stripe that lights up on selection
nesting: a flat list inside .ai2-rows (a scrolling rail), each row a link to a card's own full page
title_pattern: header bar (title, meter, path stacked with a fixed gap)
notes: a card with the corners and border sanded off so many can sit edge-to-edge in a narrow rail — same padding token as .card, deliberately no radius or full border. The AI2 board's rail-row and the clicked-through full card are the same data shown two ways.

name: decision box (layouts/browse item page)
border: box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--line) (an inset hairline, not a real border)
nesting: one per item page, standalone — not inside a wall
notes: the file's own comment calls this 'the one box on the item page, because it is the one thing the page exists for' — a deliberate single card per page, not a repeated kind.

name: accordion row (disclosure)
background: light-dark(#fff, var(--surface)); none in the 'lines' variant (a rule under each row instead of a box)
radius: 0 on the row; the stack's own wrapper can round the whole group
border: 1px solid var(--line) bottom, only in the 'flush' word
nesting: native <details>/<summary>, each one a row inside a .ux-content-stack; a stack does not nest inside another card in the files read
notes: the one expandable kind found — built on native <details>, not a custom widget. This is the piece closest to what the owner asked for next (a log group you can open), already proven for Decision/Question/Quotation/Spend.

name: object card
padding: not set directly on the rule read (inherited card padding)
border: 2px solid var(--line) (thicker than the 1px used elsewhere)
nesting: holds property chips and method chips (this inventory's 'chip' kind) inside it; sits alone in a column, max-width 32em
notes: a 2px border is unique to this one and ux-content-answer/-field — every other card in the inventory uses 1px or none; worth reconciling (see findings.md).

name: panel region
where: public/framework/ext/Panel/panel.css:1 ("what a panel LOOKS like is surface/wash off framework.css"), :59 (.panel-body), :31 (.panel); public/framework/ext/Panel/controls.css (the toolbar)
background: none of its own — a caller opts a panel into `.surface` or `.wash` (framework.css) for its ground, same tokens this inventory's other kinds share
padding: var(--panel-pad, 0) — zero unless a caller sets it; a template keeps its own inner padding on its own inner element, one layer further in
radius: none set here — comes from `.surface`/`.wash` when a caller adds one of those
border: none of its own, same reasoning as background
nesting: a workspace of panels, split by a grip into rows/columns; a panel can hold another panel (a nested split) or a template payload
title_pattern: none — a panel is unnamed until a template gives it one
notes: the toolbar (`panel-btn` row, controls.css) is this system's menu pattern: transparent until hovered (`--fill-a08`), a tinted `on` state (`color-mix(--prim 15%)`) for the pressed one — a row of icon buttons doing the job a single ⋯ menu does elsewhere, deliberately with no background of its own (the owner, 2026-08-16: chrome over content, not a bar). Missed by the three surveys that built this inventory (found in the 2026-09-29 audit, `inventory-audit.md`) because it is a page-*internal* layout system, not a directory-index card.

name: switcher (routed list + content)
where: public/framework/core/Page/layout/switcher/switcher.css:156 (nav skin active row), public/framework/ext/tabs/tabs.css:260 (.tabs.vertical default active row)
background: the list itself: none at rest; the CURRENT row is var(--fill-a08) (nav skin) or var(--tab-fill, var(--surface)) (default, no skin chosen)
padding: inherited from ext/tabs' own .tab padding — nothing extra added here
radius: var(--radius) on the current row only (nav skin); none in the default/tree skins
border: 1px solid var(--line) under the narrow-width dropdown and its sticky header; none around the list itself at normal width
nesting: a list (the switcher) beside its content (a `.tab-panel`, which is the routed child page's own render()) — at under 30em the list collapses to a one-row sticky header that opens as a dropdown over the content
title_pattern: none — the list's own rows ARE the titles
notes: three skins (tree/nav/plain), one mechanism: only which class marks the CURRENT row changes. Built 2026-09-29, after the three card-inventory surveys already ran, which is why it was missing (found in the same day's audit, `inventory-audit.md`) — a timing gap, not a blind spot in scope.
